name: Bosnia and Herzegovina (1992–1998)
description: A white field with the coat of arms of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the centre: a blue shield with a white diagonal band and six yellow fleurs-de-lis, bordered in yellow.
history: Adopted on 20 May 1992, shortly after Bosnia and Herzegovina declared independence from Yugoslavia on 3 March 1992, replacing the socialist republic's flag. The shield with the fleurs-de-lis (the 'Bosnian lily') is derived from the arms of the medieval Kotromanić dynasty. Rejected by Serb and Croat representatives after the war, it was replaced on 4 February 1998 by the present flag imposed by the High Representative, but remains in widespread unofficial use among Bosniaks.

features.role: shield with white bend and six fleurs-de-lis
